<store>
Name: Tidewell Candles
Sells: Tidewell Candles sells candles: scented container candles and unscented taper candles. The range includes an 8 oz sea salt soy candle hand-poured in Portland, Maine, a 12 oz cedar candle in a coconut and soy wax blend with a crackling cherry-wood wick, and a pair of 10-inch pure beeswax tapers made with beeswax from Maine apiaries.
Audience: People shopping for home candles who care about the wax and wick, such as soy, coconut-soy or pure beeswax, hand-poured or locally sourced in Maine.
Tone: friendly
Never say: —
</store>

<topic>
Working title: How to Reuse a Candle Jar Once the Candle Is Done
Search it targets: how to reuse candle jars
</topic>

<products>
  P1: Sea Salt Soy Candle, 8 oz (Candle)
    F1: The Sea Salt Soy Candle is 8 oz.
    F2: The Sea Salt Soy Candle is made of 100% soy wax.
    F3: The Sea Salt Soy Candle is poured by hand in Portland, Maine.
    F4: The Sea Salt Soy Candle has a cotton wick.
    F5: The Sea Salt Soy Candle's wick is lead-free.
    F6: The Sea Salt Soy Candle has a burn time of about 45 hours.
    F7: The Sea Salt Soy Candle comes in an 8 oz amber glass jar.
    F8: The Sea Salt Soy Candle's jar has a tin lid.
    F9: The Sea Salt Soy Candle has scent notes of sea salt, driftwood, and sage.
    F10: The Sea Salt Soy Candle is made by Tidewell.
  P2: Cedar Wood-Wick Candle, 12 oz (Candle)
    F11: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle is 12 oz.
    F12: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle is made by Tidewell.
    F13: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle is made with a coconut and soy wax blend.
    F14: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle has a cherry-wood wick that crackles as it burns.
    F15: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle has a burn time of about 60 hours.
    F16: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle comes in a 12 oz ceramic vessel.
    F17: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle's vessel is reusable.
    F18: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle's wick should be trimmed to 3 mm before each burn.
    F19: The Cedar Wood-Wick Candle has scent notes of cedar, black pepper, and vetiver.
</products>

content.text: {"title":"How to Reuse Candle Jars: Cleaning Tips and Second-Life Ideas","angle":"Readers will learn how to safely get leftover wax out of a finished candle jar, clean it properly, and turn it into something useful, plus which Tidewell vessels make especially good keepers.","sections":[{"heading":"When a Candle Is Really Done","covers":"General advice on stopping a burn when about half an inch of wax remains, why burning to the bottom can overheat the container, and letting the jar cool fully before working on it.","facts":[]},{"heading":"Getting the Leftover Wax Out","covers":"General methods: freezing the jar so the wax pops out, the hot-water method, and gently warming then pouring off wax. How soy and coconut-soy waxes tend to release more easily and wash up with warm soapy water. Removing the wick tab.","facts":["F2","F13"]},{"heading":"Cleaning and Removing Labels","covers":"Washing with warm soapy water, removing sticker residue with oil or baking soda paste, drying thoroughly, and tips for glass versus ceramic surfaces.","facts":[]},{"heading":"Ideas for Your Empty Jar","covers":"Reuse ideas: bathroom storage for cotton swabs, a pen or makeup brush holder, a small planter for succulents, a pantry jar for spices or tea, a vase for small stems, or refilling with new wax for a homemade candle.","facts":[]},{"heading":"Tidewell Jars Worth Keeping","covers":"Why the Sea Salt Soy Candle's amber glass jar with tin lid makes a handy lidded storage jar, and why the Cedar Wood-Wick Candle's ceramic vessel is designed to be reused, e.g. as a planter or desk cup.","facts":["F7","F8","F1","F16","F17","F11"]},{"heading":"Enjoying the Candle Before the Jar","covers":"Brief notes on getting a full burn before reuse: burn times, trimming the wood wick to 3 mm each time, and the cotton lead-free wick and scents of each candle.","facts":["F6","F15","F18","F14","F4","F5","F9","F19","F3"]}],"products":["P1","P2"],"links":["P1","P2","L1"]}
